checks: Verified 7051dc5265e081de §§1–5 in full. The source uses the original mixed length and the same weighted geometric-mean multiplier constraint; it explicitly lacks strict proper-minor quotas.

The sole integer sites are the exposed endpoint bases. After normalizing a nonvertical continuous coefficient to either sign, a finite base tilt isolates the specified own trace without changing it, and a pure-base isolator has mass V. The better axial trace has length min(V,V/2−|y|+δ). The unsaturated expression strictly decreases with |y|.
Recomputed mixed length 5/2, variance 7/48, c²=7/120, and the geometric-mean exponents 2 and 3. The product of the fourth and sixth powers of the midpoint shifts is (3/2)³(εc)¹⁰.

At q=1 the root polynomial has value 1/65536. The resulting ε cutoff power is 120⁵/(221184·7⁵). Opposite strict monotonicity on the two unsaturated branches gives uniqueness below the cutoff, with both midpoints deepest and each own cut proper.

As ε tends to zero the root tends to 3/4; the first multiplier's rescaled limit is (1/4)²/(7/120)=15/14, the other follows from the product constraint, and the limiting midpoint shifts are 1/4 and zero.

At or above the cutoff, a value below 1 would make both shifts strictly smaller than their crossing values, contradicting the product. Setting the larger interval's shift to 1/4 realizes 1. The smaller interval is captured fully at the specified optimizer, with a supporting cut at equality.
